subject: Post-call: side-by-side infra & observability tests (next steps)
messages:
From: Leah Grant <leah@cloudscale.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@hypercloud.com>, Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up + suggested test matrix

Great talking with you both earlier - thanks for the demo and the clear differentiation points. Per our discussion, CloudScale's evaluation committee wants a concise side-by-side of Redwood vs the two hyperscalers (HyperCloud and MegaServe) focusing on operational tooling: observability, tracing, dashboards, usage analytics, and cost transparency.

To keep things focused we proposed these core tests during the call:
- Latency profile: p50/p95 tail at 99th token for streaming and non-streaming scenarios (1k token generation, batch sizes 1, 8, 32)
- Tracing integration: end-to-end trace with our frontend -> Redwood -> model runtime; distributed trace spans and sampling config
- Metrics completeness: token-level cost breakdown, model and route-level token accounting, KV cache hit/miss metrics
- Dashboards: out-of-the-box dashboard for top-line SLOs + ability to build custom views (per-route, per-customer)
- Anomaly/quality alerts tied to prompt sets (we'll provide 5 seed prompts)

Can you confirm you can run these tests (or a representative subset) in a reserved short POC? If so we need: estimates for time to run, owners, and any artifacts you will provide (scripts, dashboards, instrumentation snippets). Procurement has asked for a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a preliminary PO amount so they can budget - attached is a template.

Thanks - looking to align for the internal committee meeting next Thursday.

Leah Grant
Director of Platform Engineering
CloudScale AI

---
Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf (map template)

Adding ops detail and instrumentation notes. Sharing the preliminary observability matrix (attached) - it maps each requested test to the telemetry we will capture and the dashboard widget we'll build. High level notes below.

Instrumentation & data model notes:
- Traces: we'll emit a span for the request entry (frontend), a span for routing (policy selection), and spans for model runtime: token-generation chunks (streaming) and kv-cache lookup. Sampling: default 10% but we will do 100% for the test window and provide full traces in redacted form.
- Metrics: we will surface per-request token_count, model_variant, route_id, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (0/1), latency_ms. Token-level billing CSV will include timestamps, token_count_in, token_count_out, model_version, and per-token cost estimate.
- Dashboards: out-of-the-box SLO view (p50/p95/p99), a cost-explorer that slices by route/model, and a trace-linked error explorer for quick root cause. We'll provide READ-ONLY links.
- Alerts: we will wire a simple alert that triggers on p95>800ms or token_cost_spike > 20% over baseline.

Attachments: observability-matrix.xlsx (test -> metric -> dashboard mapping).

ETA: dashboards + CSV export -> Tue 2026-05-26 EOD; traces + sample spans -> Mon 2026-05-25 EOD. Sergio and I will coordinate the perf runs to ensure stability of results.

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
